Reference.Title: FAMILY HISTORY OF ASTHMA IN INFANTS WITH BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA
Reference.Address: ARIZONA HLTH SCI CTR, DEPT PEDIAT, PEDIAT PULMONARY SECT, TUCSON, AZ 85724 USA; ARIZONA HLTH SCI CTR, DIV RESP SCI, TUCSON, AZ 85724 USA
Reference.Abstract: The role of genetic or familial factors in the development of human bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is unknown. Detailed histories concerning asthma, allergy and other lung diseases were obtained on 1st and 2nd degree relatives of 17 infants with BPD, and 21 infants who had hyaline membrane disease [HMD]. All infants in the BPD and HMD groups had HMD requiring assisted ventilation and greater than 50% inspired O2 in the 1st 5 days of life. The diagnosis of HMD and BPD were made on radiographic and clinical criteria. Of 17 infants with BPD, 13 had 1st or 2nd degree relatives with physician-diagnosed asthma, compared to 7 of 21 in the HMD group (P < .01). A significantly greater number of relatives of BPD infants (P < .005) had were hospitalized for their asthma as compared to HMD relatives. There were no differences between the groups for allergic rhinitis, eczema, bronchitis, emphysema, chronic cough, smoking or wheezing with respiratory illnesses. Airways with a genetic predisposition for reactivity may become highly reactive following neonatal lung disorders and their treatment. These irritable airways may then contribute to the development, progression or both of BPD.
